faqs.a: It depends on the animal, how it got in, and how much sealing and cleanup the job needs. Our crew inspects first, shows you the entry points we found in Newport News, and gives you a quote after inspection before any removal or sealing work begins — no prices promised over the phone.

faqs.q: When can bats be removed from a Newport News attic?
faqs.a: Bats in Virginia are handled by exclusion only — one-way exits fitted and every other opening sealed so the colony leaves on its own. Under our permit conditions the maternity season runs May 1 through August 15, and bats may not be excluded or removed then unless no young are present or there is a threat to human health or safety, so we inspect any time but schedule most Newport News exclusions outside that window. Since January 1, 2025, bat work also requires a CNAP holder with DWR-recognized bat training, which is how our crew works.

Newport News.wildlife_intro:
Newport News stretches from shipyard blocks to Denbigh suburbs, with a huge wooded park at its center in Newport News. Our crew's calls here follow the ground: james River and Hampton Roads harbor shore, Newport News Park's reservoir woods, Warwick River. Raccoons and gray squirrels take attics and chimneys, striped skunks and opossums work yards and crawlspaces, and bats settle older rooflines in summer.

In spring we remove denning raccoon and squirrel families before the young are mobile. Summer brings skunk, groundhog, and snake calls and the bat maternity season, when exclusion waits under Virginia permit conditions. Fall is sealing season in Newport News — squirrels, rats, and bats all test the same gaps looking for winter shelter, and our crew closes them after the animals are out, because sealing alone rarely holds.
